description: Photogrammetry 3D-scanning rig: a fully printed hand-rotated turntable whose platter locates on a 45-degree V-groove race and a centring spindle, with numbered 15-degree rotation tick marks against an index pointer on the base rim, plus a generic leaning phone stand whose slot width is customizable (default fits an iPhone 15 Pro, bare or cased). No non-printed hardware required. A separate link part collars the turntable base and keys into two notches in its rim, so the base can neither be dragged out from under the fixed masking ellipse nor twisted inside the collar by hand-turning the platter; its other end is a low open-top rail. The camera boost plinth stands on the desk behind that rail and carries the rig's only stand pocket, tilted nose-down. An optional riser drops into the boost's own pocket and re-presents an identical one further up, correcting the camera's elevation angle over the platter without changing the boost. A spacer inserts between the link's rail and the boost and moves the boost another 135mm back; at the 222mm platter it is required for framing, not optional.
printing_notes: All parts print support-free in their exported orientations: turntable base and platter flat on the bed, phone stand on its side face (every layer is the same cross-section).
The platter is exported groove-side down — slice it as-is so the V-groove's 45-degree walls stay self-supporting.
If the platter feels gritty to turn, work a little candle wax or PTFE lubricant into the V-groove and across the base plate's top face. Do not sand the 45-degree flanks; they set the concentricity.
The 14mm phone slot fits most cased phones; use the customizer to narrow slot_w for a snug grip on a bare phone.
For landscape scanning, slide the phone along the slot so the camera-bump corner overhangs past the end of the stand rather than resting on the backrest.

Centre the phone's rear camera roughly over the middle of the stand and confirm the platter's position in roi-preview.jpg before capturing; the mask ellipse is set per capture, so the camera does not have to sit exactly on the rig's axis.

Camera elevation is not optional polish. At the pre-#468 geometry the camera sat about 21 degrees above the platter and a uniform-grey object registered 18 of 150 continuous frames (fragmenting into 7 models) and 2 of 54 step-and-holds — near edge-on, the platter's numerals foreshorten away and only the periodic knurl is left to match. Keep the ellipse's ry/rx at 0.64 or above.

The platter's tick numerals are engraved 0.5mm into the top face. Print them at 0.2mm layers or finer, and do not sand the top face — the numerals are what makes each angular sector unique to photogrammetry feature matching.

The rig link prints flat on the bed with no supports; its 248 × 247mm footprint needs a 250mm bed — it is sized to fill a Bambu Lab A1 (256 × 256). Disable skirt and brim or the outline falls off the plate. Its rail is 12mm tall, open-topped so nothing bridges.

Drop the turntable base into the link's collar from above — the 200-degree wrap means it cannot slide out sideways, only lift straight up, and its two rim notches drop over the collar's two keys at the one rotation where they line up, which also puts the index pointer on the rig axis. The base then cannot turn inside the collar. The phone stand mounts on the scan boost; the link itself carries no stand pocket.

The turntable base has three 12mm x 1.2mm recesses in its underside for stick-on rubber or TPU anti-slip pads. They print as short bridges a couple of layers above the bed — no support needed. Set foot_pads false in the customizer for a plain flat underside.

The optional scan boost prints flat on the bed with no supports, exactly as exported — every wall rises off the bed and the hollow core closes in at under 45 degrees. At the default 26mm setback behind the rail and 90mm pocket-floor height it is about 119mm long and 130mm tall (160mm including the saddle arms). It is taller than the pre-#486 boost, so an existing boost does not fit the scaled rig.

Fit the boost by standing it on the desk behind the rig link and sliding it forward until its saddle arms straddle the rail and its front wall meets the rail's rear face. It is the rig's only stand mount. On its own, boost_floor_h (25-110mm) alone only puts the camera at about 34 degrees above the platter (ry/rx 0.55) — under the 0.64 ry/rx floor; fit the scan riser (below) for a usable elevation.

The optional scan riser prints flat on the bed with no supports, solid apart from its own top pocket. It drops into the boost's existing pocket exactly where the phone stand's foot sat before — same fit, same kerb — then re-presents an identical pocket riser_h higher for the phone stand to drop into instead. riser_h = 140mm, about 146mm tall; drop the phone stand's foot straight into it once it is seated.

The riser is the rig's camera-elevation adjustment: riser_h = 140mm on the 90mm boost puts the camera at about 55 degrees (ry/rx 0.82) with the boost and riser alone, and about 41 degrees (0.66) with the setback spacer at its 135mm default — the configuration the rig is sized for.

At boost + riser height the stack is a tower with a phone leaning back on top — keep the desk footprint behind it clear and don't knock it mid-capture. Never link the boost or riser to the platter; it must stay free to turn.
The optional setback spacer prints flat on the bed with no supports: its floor plate lands on the bed, every wall rises off it and the top is open. At the default 135mm shift it is 175 × 47 × 12mm.

Fit the spacer by dropping its saddle over the rig link's rail, then sliding the scan boost back until its saddle straddles the spacer's rail and its front wall meets the rail's rear end wall. Not optional at the 222mm platter: without it the platter fills ~79% of frame width and can clip the frame edge; with it, ~63% — the headroom the 150mm platter had.
Customize the setback spacer with the same rail_w and rail_h as the rig link and the boost, or its rail will not match the boost's saddle.

The 222mm platter and 238mm base are large flat prints — expect several hours each and a well-levelled bed; a brim on the base helps if the pad-recess corners lift. This is a scale-up for a 250mm bed (#486): only the phone stand is unchanged from v2.1.0 — the base, platter, link, boost, riser and spacer all need reprinting.
